newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firm but pare gains with Btps.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firm but pare gains with Btps.

text.p: Italian shares ended firm on Thursday but slipped back from higher levels in late trade, in the wake of a correction in Btp bond futures, with profit-taking seen on selected major stocks after both the Mib30 blue chip index and the Fib30 futures index had again touched new highs, dealers said.
"We're at rather critical levels now and at this point the Bourse is becoming very sensitive, as it was today to Btps which started the rally on Wednesday," one trader said.
The All-share Mibtel index closed up 0.99 percent at 13,058 after a session high of 13,170 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended up 1.11 percent at 19,829 after a 20.027 high.

The June contract on the Fib30 stock futures index rose to a fresh record high of 20,065 in afternoon trade, breaking the psychological 20,000 level. The contract, which expires Friday, was 240 basis points up on the day at 19,850 by 1520 GMT.
Among blue chips moving into negative territory were Fiat, off 0.59 percent to 6,100 lire, and mobile phone operator TIM, down 0.07 percent at 5,535.
Dealers saw block trades of 26 million Fiat shares over Wednesday and today ahead of the future and options expiries.
Olivetti slipped 0.09 percent to 462.1 lire and in banks Ambroveneto lost 0.89 percent to 4,450. Financial holding Gemina fell 4.75 percent to 527.8.
Among major gainers, clothing group Benetton put on 3.43 percent to 27,434 lire, insurer Mediolanum rose 3.96 percent to 18,225, and Pirelli Spa gained 3.5 percent to 4,285.
Total traded volume was estimated at nearly double Wednesday's at some 2.09 trillion lire.
